1000634.etyen: Calque of German Österreich (“Austria”), equivalent to øster (“east, eastward”) + rike (“realm, country”), literally “eastern realm”. The German form continues Middle High German Osterīche (“Austria”), from Old High German Ōstarrīhhi (“eastern realm”), attested since 996 and formed from ōstar (“east, eastward”) and rīhhi (“realm, land”). The first element derives from Proto-Germanic *austraz (“east, eastern”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éwsteros (“eastern”), ultimately from the root *h₂ews- (“dawn, east”). The second element derives from Proto-West Germanic *rīkī (“realm”), from Proto-Germani

1004986.etyen:
Compound of etter (“after”) + sikt (“sight, presentation”) + kurs (“rate, exchange rate”), with linking -s- (“interfix”) between sikt and kurs, literally “after-sight exchange rate”.
The first element, etter (“after”), is inherited from Old Norse eptir (“after”), from Proto-Germanic *after (“after, behind”), ultimately from a Proto-Indo-European formation meaning “further behind, further away”. The second element, sikt (“sight, presentation”), is from German Sicht (“sight, view”), from Middle High German siht (“sight”), from Old High German siht (“sight”), ultimately from the Proto-Indo-Europe
